lead: Quantum states are lists of complex numbers, so complex arithmetic and complex vector spaces decide what a qubit can do. A complex vector space is the real vector space you know with complex scalars. That change makes rotation free, doubles dimension over R, and makes independence subtler. Amplitude, phase and interference live here.
prereq: You need first-year engineering mathematics: real vectors, real matrices, basic trigonometry. Section 1.1 explains why physics uses complex amplitudes.

sections.h3: Complex numbers: two real numbers and one rule

blocks.text: A complex number is z = a + bi. a is Re(z), b is Im(z), both real. The symbol i obeys i² = −1. So z is a pair (a, b) with a multiplication rule.
Addition adds parts: (a + bi) + (c + di) = (a + c) + (b + d)i. Multiplication expands and replaces i² by −1.

blocks.where: a, b, c, d are real; ac − bd is the real part of the product and ad + bc is the imaginary part.

blocks.text: The conjugate flips the imaginary sign: z̄ = a − bi. The modulus is length |z| = √(a² + b²). Then z z̄ = a² + b² = |z|², real and ≥ 0, zero only for z = 0. Division: z / w = z w̄ / |w|².
For z = 3 + 4i, |z| = √(9 + 16) = 5. It is a plane point, 3 right and 4 up. Quantum amplitudes are such points, so 1 + (−1) cancels but 1 + i does not.

sections.h3: Polar form and why i is a quarter turn

blocks.text: Polar form names a point by distance and angle. Let r = |z| ≥ 0 and θ = arg z be the anticlockwise angle from the positive real axis in radians. Then a = r cos θ, b = r sin θ, and Euler gives z = r(cos θ + i sin θ) = r e<sup>iθ</sup>.
z = r e<sup>iθ</sup> = r(cos θ + i sin θ)
blocks.where: r = |z| = √(a² + b²) is the modulus and θ = arg z is the argument in radians; θ + 2πk gives the same z for every whole number k.

blocks.text: Multiplication multiplies lengths and adds angles: z₁z₂ = r₁r₂ e<sup>i(θ₁+θ₂)</sup>. Since i = e<sup>iπ/2</sup>, multiplying by i keeps length and adds π/2 rad. Multiplication by i is a quarter turn.
Phase gates rotate amplitude arrows. Section 3 uses the same quarter turn to decide independence.

sections.h3: Vector spaces over C, span, independence, dimension

blocks.text: A vector space over C is a set V with addition u + v and complex scalar multiplication cv, obeying the usual nine rules: closure; u + v = v + u; (u + v) + w = u + (v + w); a zero vector; an inverse −v; 1v = v; c(u + v) = cu + cv; (c + d)v = cv + dv; (cd)v = c(dv).
The standard example is Cⁿ: ordered n-tuples (z₁, …, zₙ), added and scaled coordinate by coordinate. C² is one qubit's state space (Unit 2, Qubits, Postulates and Entanglement).

A linear combination is c₁v₁ + … + cₖvₖ with cⱼ in C. Its span is all such combinations. v₁, …, vₖ are independent if c₁v₁ + … + cₖvₖ = 0 forces all cⱼ = 0. A basis is an independent spanning set. Dimension is its size; every basis has the same size. Thus dim Cⁿ = n over C.

In C² take v = (1, i), w = (i, −1). Try w = cv. The first coordinate gives c = i. The second gives ci = i² = −1, which matches. So w = i v and {v, w} is dependent over C. Over R, a v + b w = 0 gives a + bi = 0 and ai − b = 0, so a = b = 0. Same vectors, independent over R. Check the allowed field.

figure.caption: Multiplying v = (1, i) by i gives w = (i, −1). The matching row proves dependence over C.

spec.title: w equals i times v
spec.aria: v = (1, i), w = (i, −1), and i times v = (i, −1); the last two rows match, so w = i v and the vectors are dependent over C.

examples.question: In C² let v = (1, i) and w = (i, −1). (a) Find a complex scalar c with w = cv. (b) Is {v, w} independent over C? (c) Is it independent over R? (d) Give |c| and the rotation angle.
steps: Suppose w = cv, so (i, −1) = c(1, i) = (c, ci).
Second coordinate: ci = i · i = i² = −1, which matches w.
So c = i ≠ 0 and w = i v. The set {v, w} is dependent over C.
Over R, set a v + b w = 0. This gives (a + bi, ai − b) = (0, 0), so a = b = 0. The set is independent over R.
c = i has |c| = 1 and angle θ = π/2 rad = 90°, so c rotates by a quarter turn.
examples.answer: c = i gives w = i v, so {v, w} is dependent over C but independent over R; |c| = 1 and the rotation is π/2 rad (90°).
examples.check:
v = (1 + 0j, 0 + 1j)
w = (0 + 1j, -1 + 0j)
c = w[0] / v[0]
p = c * v[1]
print(c.real)
print(c.imag)
print(p.real)
print(p.imag)
print(abs(c))

traps: Independence depends on allowed scalars: (1, i) and (i, −1) are independent over R, dependent over C.
Conjugate is not negative: a + bi has conjugate a − bi, while its negative is −a − bi.
Modulus is not square: |3 + 4i| = 5, not 25; |z|² = z z̄.
Euler form has period 2π: θ and θ + 2π give the same z; e<sup>iθ</sup> is never 0.
Dimension depends on field: Cⁿ is n over C but 2n over R.

quiz.q: Define i, Re(z) and Im(z), and state i².
quiz.a: i² = −1. For z = a + bi with a, b real, Re(z) = a and Im(z) = b.

quiz.q: List any four axioms of a vector space over C.
quiz.a: Any four: closure; u + v = v + u; associativity; zero vector; inverse −v; 1v = v; c(u + v) = cu + cv; (c + d)v = cv + dv; (cd)v = c(dv).

quiz.q: Use polar form to explain why multiplying by i rotates by 90°.
quiz.a: z = r e<sup>iθ</sup> and i = e<sup>iπ/2</sup>, so iz = r e<sup>i(θ+π/2)</sup>. Length r is unchanged and angle grows by π/2 rad = 90°.

quiz.q: Write z = 1 + i in polar form.
quiz.a: r = √2 ≈ 1.414 and θ = π/4 rad = 45°, so z = √2 e<sup>iπ/4</sup>.

quiz.q: Are u = (1, 1) and t = (i, i) independent over C? Give the scalar.
quiz.a: t = i u, so c = i ≠ 0 and the set is dependent over C.

quiz.q: Give dim C³ over C and over R, and explain.
quiz.a: Over C it is 3. Over R each complex coordinate needs two real numbers, so it is 6 = 2 × 3.

quiz.q: A student says (1, i) and (i, −1) are independent because no real multiple links them. Correct the error.
quiz.a: That is true only over R. In a complex space i(1, i) = (i, −1), so they are dependent over C.

beyond: Not for the exam. Quantum programs store states as complex arrays, often 64-bit or 128-bit complex floats. Simulation cost is mostly complex multiplication. Error-corrected hardware also needs fast complex arithmetic in decoders. Search next for complex vector space qubit, Euler formula phase gate, and numpy complex128 statevector.
